title: The Synergy of Wills and the Crucifixion of the Self
english: "Long-lasting on the good earth, which the Lord God gives to you." If you were to take [this] regarding this earth and these immediate parents, it is a lie. Regarding the present [text], it is not said "which he gives to you."

"Stop your tongue from evil." He calls you to learn the fear of the Lord, so that having learned, you may become holy, undefiled, lacking no virtue. Therefore come, so that you may stop your tongue from evil. Let the tongue of the inner man no longer have evil. Then indeed it becomes all outward, when it has and brings forth the good. And it follows the stopping of the tongue from evil and the lips no longer speaking deceit, and it also calms the hypocrisy; for one who acts deceitfully is to do evil.

"Their tongue is a piercing arrow, deceitful are the words of their mouth." These are those from the heresies, those who stand before ungodliness. One can therefore say regarding the explicit [text]: since at that time especially when we say this, all were running toward evil, as for the remainder to sing laments over them, he was saying toward such people: for he did not say "each of my brothers" or "each of our brothers", that is, of the saints, but of those desiring to have one father, those born of the devil through wanting to do his desires; for "you are of the father the devil and you want to do the desires of the devil."

Regarding such brothers, born for the father and the evil one, he says: "every brother stumbles"; for indeed their father is such: by deceit he led all under himself and leads those following him by wickedness. "And every friend" is such [that he] "will fall". He is not speaking about those who are truly friends. Jesus says to the disciples: "You are friends"; and he gave the reason: "because all things of the father I have made known to you." None of these friends will fall. Because of this they are free. Therefore the word is toward those who are such: "they will by no means speak truth." Regarding those not speaking truth, the word is: "he did not stand in the truth." He who is not standing in the truth has once been in it. But we never say about anyone that he does not stand in a craft, unless he has been tested in a craft or in many crafts and...

He might pass from one [state] to another. If he had not become one in the truth, not standing in it would not have brought him reproach. And behold the doctrine: how 'God wants all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth' (1 Tim 2:4)? If no one opposes His will, how is it that some are lagging behind, despite His wanting all to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth—so that I may not say, the majority? If He wants [it], and if we also want [it], and a convergence of the two wills occurs, salvation happens; for no one is good against his will, no one who does not want is saved, and no one hurrying toward approaching God and having kept His law is able to know the truth.

For this reason also the Savior says in the Gospel: 'If anyone wants to come after me, let him deny himself and let him take up his cross and follow me' (Matt 16:24). 'If anyone wants': as far as it concerns the Savior, He wills him to do this, but He does not compel; He moves the choice, He awakens the desire. 'If anyone' therefore 'wants to come after me', 'if anyone wants to follow me'—for this is what 'to come after me' means—, 'let him take up his own cross': let him be crucified to the world, let him put to death 'his members which are upon the earth', let him become inactive toward the world. He who is crucified has his feet hindered from walking as he wants, and his hands from doing what he wants. Therefore, when someone is crucified toward the world, he neither walks according to it anymore, nor does he do its things; and by this, the world is also crucified to the one crucified, so that the world may also be inactive toward him, neither walking according to him, nor doing those things that harm him.

'If anyone' therefore 'wants to come after me': perhaps not, perhaps yes; for virtue, when spoken of continuously, is virtue and perfection, not as in other actions. Just so also the apostle writes: 'Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, giving thanks in all circumstances' (1 Thess 5:16-18). He who rejoices always possesses the virtue always; for he rejoices not upon anything else except upon being well-pleasing in the pleasing God. 'Loving to see good days' (Ps 90:16). The 'to see' here means to be tested, and 'to be tested of good days' means to enjoy. 'Keep your tongue from evil'. Let your word be restrained, let it be tested; let it desire to have an unsearchable word; as it writes...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Pursuit of Righteousness and the Nature of God
english: The apostle calls the 'healthy word' 'unfailing' (ἀκατάγνωστον). He who possesses an unfailing word fulfills many commandments of Jesus. It is impossible for one not possessing an unfailing word to keep that: 'Let your yes be yes and your no, no' (Matt 5:37); for one who is not believing is sometimes required to swear an oath. But if one always possesses a word that is not scrutinized, no one ever doubts him, whether he previously tells the truth or not, or whether he says and does as he says, when an oath is required and his yes is yes and his no is no, such a word is indeed unfailing. Again, he who goes through the doctrines of the truth and demonstrates them scientifically possesses a word and is unfailing concerning them. No one is able to accuse him of lying, of thinking poorly, or of being outside the truth.

Turn away from evil and do good (Rom 12:21). This says: if you happen to be in evil, if you are settled in it and acting according to it, since I call you to the doing of the good, turn away from the evil. It is impossible to be outside both. Let the infants be circumcised now (cf. Acts 7:50). He who is not in good is in evil; he who happens to be outside of evil participates in the good. Therefore, 'turn away from evil.' And the turning is a matter of choice, for it protects and advises. But no one protects or advises one who does not have choice. I call you to do the good. You cannot do it otherwise and act according to it, unless you turn away from the evil. Thus also it is said in Isaiah: 'Stop from your evils, learn to do good' (Isa 1:16); for as long as anyone is in his evils, that is, his wickedness, he is acting [in them], and this one is unable to learn to do good. Again the law-giving apostle writes: 'Test all things, hold fast to the good, abstain from every form of evil' (1 Thess 5:21-22). Therefore also, 'turn away from evil and do good.' It is not sufficient to turn away from evil unless one also does the good; for it is possible to turn away from evil being prevented by fear of punishment from going toward this, but this one does not do the good by choice; for if you bypass the good by will, it is no longer at all good.
Seek peace and pursue it (Ps 34:14). Evil is a crowding thing and works turmoil in the soul; for the race of wickedness has much difference...

Evil things occur either in a small way or in excess, such as cowardice and rashness, or superstition and impiety. One must pursue peace; for to pursue it in this way does not mean that one has driven it away. You have this also in the Proverbs: 'those pursuing,' it is said, 'love righteousness' (Proverbs 15:27), meaning that God clearly loves them, that is, those who pursue. The righteousness that is pursued is all virtue. For Wisdom says: 'Evil men will seek me and will not find me' (Proverbs 1:28). The evil men seek wisdom only to hide it and make it vanish, as much as it reaches them. But those eager to become wise do not seek wisdom in this way, but they pursue it.

And I say, since you love these interpretive things: Herod sought Jesus in order to kill him. Often the Jews sought him in order to kill him. But the disciples sought him in order to be benefited, in order to partake of him. For someone said to him: 'The crowds seek to see you,' because they wanted to believe and see paradoxical works and hear words and chance upon healings. Therefore, 'pursuing' is a homonym.

16 For the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous (Psalm 34:15). Much exhortation again, much instruction. This is what it says: the eyes of God are ready to see and save, and his ears are ready to obey. 'Turn away' therefore 'from evil and do good, and seek peace and pursue it' (Psalm 34:14); for immediately you will have God as a supporter. Only desire to be righteous, to pursue righteousness, and you have the eyes of God lying upon you and his ears ready to receive the requests which you make to him. 16 And his ears toward their prayers.

Often it has been said that what is spoken of humans regarding God must not be taken literally, as they think it is anthropomorphic; for they want there to be a human face concerning God, and they say that the man made according to the image and likeness of God has become so according to the construction of the body. But such a thing has been overturned by wise men; for they say: 'If by this the man is according to the image of God, because he imitates God physically and his body has a likeness to God, how then is God said to have wings: "In the shelter of your wings you will protect me" (Psalm 17:8)?' Therefore, a wingless being is the...

title: The Nature of the Wicked Death
english: Man is such that he is not, according to the body, 'in image and likeness' of God. But if you reflect upon what the wings of God are, you will see that man also possesses such wings, intellectual ones, suspending him. Again, the eyes: since they take in all things according to history, the man having two eyes is not 'in image and likeness' of the One having seven, so that those things being lifted up from the sensible, the things concerning man being lifted up from the sensible, they preserve the likeness toward God.

And the face of the Lord is upon those doing evil (Ps 70:1). This he says because those doing evil are not righteous. And not being righteous, they are not feared by God, nor are they heard. However, they do not remain invisible to him. But when they fall into certain calamities and come to a realization that because of the evil things being done and thought they have come to these, they receive a vision of him. For Moses also pursued Pharaoh and his whole army with great speed, and he said he heard of God saying: 'I shall be glorified in Pharaoh and in all his army, and the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord'; for how did they know? Having become submerged, no longer being able to escape, they received a vision of God. And it is set forth in the Psalms: 'Let them be ashamed and be confounded and perish, and let them know that your name, O Lord' (Ps 76:10). After the perishing, after the being ashamed, they knew God, and this is to be the appearing of him to be and to have a face upon those doing evil.

But how else does he say: 'And you turned your face, and I became troubled' (Ps 31:7)? Elsewhere it is said: the voice belongs to the Savior. Listen then: to turn the face he does not say is from those doing evil, but from those having it appearing to them. And having been slightly troubled, they thought it was happening outside the face; therefore also they were troubled. I perceived by sense that something unpleasant was above them. And the turning of the face happened thus, toward stirring up those who previously saw him and did not have him turned away, so that they might encounter him. But for those doing evil, neither is this the cause, but so that they may perceive that by the providence of God they were judged, that by the providence of God they are in calamities. And this also happens to...

The end is useful; 17 to destroy their memory from the earth. It is not merely 'their memory', but 'from the earth', so that they are no longer counted as belonging to the earth, no longer thinking of earthly things. Just as we say that he drove this man out of the country where many prostitutions are; for it is no curse that one should remove him from there, having placed him among the opposites. 18 The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them. And rightly so, since he has ears toward them; having cried out, they happened to find him listening. Pay attention, for two things are said, one praiseworthy and one punishing; 124 it is praiseworthy that the eyes of the Lord and the ears are toward the righteous, but the face of the Lord is punishing 'to destroy the memory from the earth'; for even if the end is not a decrease, but happens through evil, it is like through cauteries and surgeries and very sharp draughts.

Regarding the other thing, the preceding says: since the ears of God are toward the prayer of the righteous and his eyes watch over them, having cried out they did not fail; for he 'heard' 'them'. And toward the other: 'the face of the Lord toward those doing evil', in the following he says: 'but the death of sinners is evil'. Not every death is evil, but the death of the sinners. And the word is not now about the common man; for that is of a living being, not of one doing, not of a sinner, not of a righteous man. Even if you call him common, when he dies as a sinner, he has an evil death—for he will receive punishment—and if the other, that which is truly appropriate to the sinner, 'sin', he says, 'having been completed, brings forth death'. But sin is completed not from outside those doing it, but in the men doing it. Therefore the death following them is evil.

And regarding the former meaning, we say the death is evil as a maker of evil, as a corruptor. But here we say evil according to the second attribution, that it is outside of goodness. The grammarians therefore read evil as 'evil as a corruptor'. 'And all the evil diseases of Egypt I will not let touch you', the grievous plagues which the Egyptians suffered according to history. And when he says: 'abstain from every form of evil', we do not say...
